problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+4y={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

The corresponding homogeneous equation has the fundamental solutions ${y}_{1}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$ 

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

According to the method of variation of parameters, we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={{field-1}}
$$

where ${u}_{1}={u}_{1}(x),{u}_{2}={u}_{2}(x),$ that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-2}}.
$$

Differentiating ${y}_{p}$ with respect to $x,$ we obtain

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore, we have the following constraint equation relating ${u}_{1}^{′}$ and ${u}_{2}^{′}:$

$$
{{field-4}}
$$
worked_solution:
Given a second-order linear inhomogeneous differential equation, the variation of parameters method requires that we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={u}_{1}(x){y}_{1}(x)+{u}_{2}(x){y}_{2}(x)
$$

that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}{y}_{1}^{′}+{u}_{2}{y}_{2}^{′}.
$$

Here, ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly independent solutions of the corresponding homogeneous equation, and ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are functions to be determined.

In this case, we're told that the fundamental solutions are

$$
{y}_{1}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x),\,{y}_{2}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our expression for ${y}_{p},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}={u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our constraint equation for ${y}_{p}^{′},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))^{′}+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))^{′}.
$$

We can form a constraint that relates ${u}_{1}^{′}$ and ${u}_{2}^{′}$ by differentiating ${y}_{p}$ and equating this expression to our constraint on ${y}_{p}^{′}.$

Differentiating ${y}_{p}$ with respect to $x$ using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={({u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))}^{′} \\  & ={({u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))}^{′}+{({u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))}^{′} \\  & ={u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+{u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))^{′}+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))^{′} \\  & ={u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we equate our two expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ={u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))^{′}+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))^{′} \\ {u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & =2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) \\ {u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\cancel{2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-\cancel{2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)} & =\cancel{2{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}-\cancel{2{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}\end{aligned}
$$

which finally gives

$$
{u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=0.
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a second-order linear inhomogeneous differential equation, the variation of parameters method requires that we seek a particular solution of the form yp(x)=u1(x)y1(x)+u2(x)y2(x) that satisfies the constraint yp′=u1y1′+u2y2′. Here, y1 and y2 are linearly independent solutions of the corresponding homogeneous equation, and u1 and u2 are functions to be determined.

In this case, we're told that the fundamental solutions are

y1=sin⁡(2x),y2=cos⁡(2x).

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our expression for yp, we get

yp=u1sin⁡(2x)+u2cos⁡(2x).

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our constraint equation for yp′, we get

yp′=u1(sin⁡(2x))′+u2(cos⁡(2x))′.

We can form a constraint that relates u1′ and u2′ by differentiating yp and equating this expression to our constraint on yp′.

Differentiating yp with respect to x using the product rule, we obtain

yp′=(u1sin⁡(2x)+u2cos⁡(2x))′=(u1sin⁡(2x))′+(u2cos⁡(2x))′=u1′sin⁡(2x)+u1(sin⁡(2x))′+u2′cos⁡(2x)+u2(cos⁡(2x))′=u1′sin⁡(2x)+2u1cos⁡(2x)+u2′cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x).

Finally, we equate our two expressions for yp′, and simplify:

u1′sin⁡(2x)+2u1cos⁡(2x)+u2′cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x)=u1(sin⁡(2x))′+u2(cos⁡(2x))′u1′sin⁡(2x)+2u1cos⁡(2x)+u2′cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x)=2u1cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x)u1′sin⁡(2x)+2u1cos⁡(2x)+u2′cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x)=2u1cos⁡(2x)−2u2sin⁡(2x) which finally gives u1′sin⁡(2x)+u2′cos⁡(2x)=0.
